name: 별 봉인 돌뚜껑(닫힘, 2×2) (star seal)
label: atlas_biome_interior/plus/star seal
reasons: 화풍: 윤곽이 근흑(재질 어두운 톤 아님) (4/4)

surfaces.part: stone lid plate with star seal inlay

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a full 30px-wide square over rows 2-30. The frame is a uniform bevel on all four sides, with light rows 3-4 at the top and rows 28-29 at the bottom. The dark inner field and the gold and purple star are seen straight from above. No vertical south face of 3 or more rows is drawn, so it is a flat plate seen top-down. That fits the flat kind and is consistent with a flat decal or plate.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts favour the candidate: 16 visible tones per tile against 3 for grass and 7 for paving, and 0% near-flat coverage. Those numbers come from a very small, busy 2x2 object, not from deep ramps. By eye, the stone frame has about 3-4 value steps and the star about 3, with only 19 colours in total. The reference paving has about 6 steps, with per-stone shading and chipped highlights. The candidate is a dark, nearly neutral rim wrapped around the whole lid, and 100% of its dark edge pixels are neutral. That reads as a uniform black sticker outline, not a dark tone of the neighbouring material. The paving reference is also mostly neutral, but only because its stone is grey, and it separates its stones by value instead of by a drawn line. The candidate has some grain and no large flat fills, but its stone surface carries less per-stone shading and texture than the reference. The uniform near-black outline and shallower ramps are enough to fail it.

surfaces.part: stone lid slab seen from above with dark inner recess and star emblem
purple and gold star seal emblem

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a 30x29 square (rows 2-30, constant width 30). It is a framed slab seen straight from above: a light stone border (rows 3-4 and 28-29), a dark inner recess, and a star emblem in the centre. The top and bottom borders are symmetric, with no front-edge line, no eave shadow, and no vertical south face. Because the object is flat on the ground, the lack of a front face is expected, but it reads as a top-down slab and not a 3/4 volume.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small boxed stone lid with a purple star, so it reads as a sticker-like prop rather than a ground patch. Its dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral (a black/grey line), and the box is wrapped in a uniform near-black outline. The paving reference separates its stones by value and tinted tone instead. The stone body has about 4 grey steps with little per-stone grain or speckle, against about 6 in the paving. The measured 16 visible tones per tile and 0% flat coverage are high, but they come from the star, gold trim and outline contrast on a very small piece. The stone surface itself is not rich. The uniform black outline and shallow stone shading look thinner than the references, so I fail it.

surfaces.part: stone lid slab with star seal inlay, seen from above as a square plate
purple and gold star emblem on lid

answer.evidence: The object is a 30x29 square plate seen straight from above. A light stone border runs around the edge (rows 3-4 at the top, rows 28-29 at the bottom) and the dark slab interior holds a purple and gold star. The width stays 30 px from row 2 to row 30, so there is no ellipse or widening profile. There is no vertical south face and no eave or front-edge line, only a thin outline at the bottom. This is a flat floor decal with no front face, which suits the flat kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small framed lid with a purple star, and it reads like a sticker. The measured facts back this up: 100% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is a near-black or grey line with no brown or material tint. The paving reference is at 80% on the same measure but is built from stone-toned shading. The candidate has 19 distinct colours in total against 80 for the grass reference. Its 16 visible tones per tile look high only because the tile holds a dense mix of frame, star and dark edge. Judged by eye, the lid body has about 4 lightness steps, with a bevelled frame and a star highlight, against 5-6 per material in Beodeul. It has no per-stone shading, speckle or grain like the paving reference's stone-by-stone texture. There are no large flat fills (near-flat coverage 0%), but the surface is smooth, not textured. The neutral near-black outline and the shallower ramps mean it would look flatter than the references beside them.

surfaces.part: stone lid slab with a beveled frame (the whole 30x29 square)

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a full 30px-wide square from rows 2 to 30, with no change in width. The border is a uniform frame on all four sides: a light bevel at rows 3-4, a dark inner frame, and a thin light/dark edge at rows 28-30. Rows 28-30 mirror the top border and do not form a south face with its own shading, so there is no front face of 3 or more rows. The interior is a flat dark slab with a star inlay, drawn straight from above. This matches a flat floor plate seen from above, so it is a top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small framed lid with a purple star on a dark slate surround. Its 16 visible tones per tile beat the references (3 and 7), but they come from a tiny 19-colour palette spent mostly on the frame, star and bevel. The stone itself has only about 3-4 lightness steps and little per-stone shading or grain compared with the paving reference, where each stone is shaded one by one. All of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral (100%), so the outline is a uniform near-black line around the whole shape. That is the 'sticker' look, not the dark material tone Beodeul uses. There are no flat 5x5 fills (0%), so texture is acceptable, but the outline and shallow ramps fall short of the Beodeul standard.
